meta.purpose: A formal ontology of the categories used throughout Masri-LLM: token classes, lexical-status classes, and normalization-operation classes, plus the decision procedures that assign them. This is meant to be read and stabilized BEFORE generating substantially more training data — every category name used in build_dataset.py's `category` field, augment_with_claude.py's generation prompt, source/lexicon.json's `loanword_status` field, and validate_output.py's token classifier should trace back to an id defined here. If a script or data file introduces a category name that isn't in this ontology, that's a signal to either add it here first (with a definition and decision procedure) or fix the script — not to let ad-hoc category names accumulate the way dataset_stats.json's stale category names did before the Aug 2026 audit.
meta.status: v1 — formalizes decision frameworks already present informally in masri_tier2_system_prompt.md, tier2-rules.json, and source/changelog.md. Not yet exhaustively cross-checked against every existing category string in the codebase — that reconciliation is the next step before scaling data generation.

token_classes.description: Input token written in Arabic script (with or without diacritics).
Input token written in Latin script using Franco/Arabizi conventions (digit-substituted phonemes, informal spelling).
Input or output token in Masri Tier 1 (ASCII-compatible, simplified) orthography.
Canonical output token in Masri Tier 2 (Coptic/Greek/Latin-extended) orthography — the system's target register.

A token that is genuine English code-switching: the speaker intends the English word AS English, spelling preserved as typed. Distinguished from egyptianized_loanword by the decision procedure `dp_codeswitch_vs_loanword` below.
A foreign-origin word phonologically and/or morphologically adapted into Egyptian Arabic, spelled per Masri rules (not preserved in original orthography).

A foreign stem that keeps its original (unadapted) spelling but has Egyptian grammatical morphology bound directly to it with no space — distinct from both pure code-switch (no morphology attached) and full egyptianized_loanword (stem itself respelled). Added to the ontology per source/changelog.md's 2026-08-20 'asave' finding; still PROVISIONAL as a named class.
A name (person, place, brand) — spelling policy may differ from common-noun loanword policy; not yet formally specified beyond 'preserve as typed' default.
A token representing a genuine numeric value (quantity, clock time, price, count) — never decoded as a phoneme-digit. See rule_zero below.

A foreign-origin token the system cannot confidently classify into any of the above. Default handling: preserve as typed, do not invent an Egyptianized spelling (see decision procedure dp_unknown_word below).

lexical_status_classes.description: A common or reliably attested Egyptian lexical form with a canonical Masri representation, present in source/lexicon.json with confidence=established.

A known alternative spelling/input form that should normalize to an established canonical form. Includes PROVISIONAL entries pending confirmation (e.g. 'escript' in source/lexicon.json) — provisional status is tracked via the entry's own confidence field, not a separate lexical_status_class.
Genuine English (or other foreign-language) code-switch: spelling preserved as typed, not normalized into Masri orthography at all beyond capitalization/punctuation conventions.
Not confidently any of the above. Default behavior per dp_unknown_word: preserve the foreign spelling, do not hallucinate a canonical form, optionally flag for the user.

normalization_operations.description: Convert spelling/script to canonical Masri Tier 2. ALWAYS apply — this is the system's core function.

Resolve ambiguous or lossy input spelling to the correct underlying phoneme sequence before applying orthographic rules. Apply WHEN pronunciation is recoverable from context/lexicon; do not guess blindly.
Preserve morphological information (tense, person, number, gender, derivation) present in the input. PRESERVE if linguistically meaningful — do not strip or simplify.

Preserve word order and sentence structure exactly as input, even when an alternative order is more frequent/idiomatic. PRESERVE if grammatically valid — this is masri_tier2_system_prompt.md's Core principle extended to syntax; see the 'Eh elli tamm?' vs 'Elli tamm eh?' example in the original project brief.
Preserve meaning exactly. ALWAYS apply, no exceptions — this is the operation every other operation is subordinate to.

rule_zero.statement: A digit must never survive in canonical Masri output as a phoneme letter-substitute. A digit may appear in output ONLY when it represents a genuine number (token_class = number). See masri_tier2_system_prompt.md 'Rule 0' for the authoritative statement; scripts/build_dataset.py's `_assert_rule_zero()` and scripts/validate_output.py's glued-digit check are the two mechanical enforcement points.

decision_procedures.question: Is a foreign-origin token english_codeswitch, egyptianized_loanword, or bound_morphology_on_unadapted_stem?
procedure: 1. Is Egyptian grammatical morphology (prefix/suffix/plural/derivation) bound directly to the stem with no space?
NO  -> is the stem itself respelled per Egyptian phonology (not just typed as English)?
YES -> egyptianized_loanword (confidence per lexicon.json entry, or 'uncertain' if unlisted)
YES -> is the STEM itself respelled (egyptianized) or kept in original spelling?
respelled -> egyptianized_loanword (morphology + respelling both present, e.g. bitza/bitzat)
original spelling kept -> bound_morphology_on_unadapted_stem (e.g. 'asave') — PROVISIONAL class, flag for review each time it's produced until formally adopted
decision_procedures.source: source/changelog.md 2026-08-20 entries; original project brief Section 4-5

decision_procedures.question: Is a digit in Franco/Arabizi input an arithmographeme (phoneme substitute) or a genuine number?
procedure: 1. Is the digit glued to Latin letters (no surrounding space/punctuation)?
YES -> arithmographeme -> decode per Rule 0's phoneme mapping, never surfaces as a digit in output
NO  -> standalone token -> is it followed by/adjacent to a countable noun or currency word?
YES -> genuine number -> keep as numeral (or spell out if the surrounding convention calls for it, e.g. clock time — see source/numeral_disambiguation_examples.json item num-05, unresolved)
NO/ambiguous -> default to the arithmographeme reading if sentence context is otherwise Franco; flag low confidence

decision_procedures.question: Encountered a foreign-origin token not in source/lexicon.json and not matching any established pattern.
procedure: 1. Do NOT invent an Egyptianized spelling.
2. Preserve the token's original spelling (treat as english_codeswitch by default).
3. Flag uncertainty to the user/caller rather than silently guessing (masri_tier2_system_prompt.md Behavior section: 'Never invent new spellings for rules not covered here').

decision_procedures.question: Should input be orthographically normalized only, or does an operation risk crossing into unwanted grammatical/syntactic rewriting?
procedure: 2. Do NOT apply any change that would alter word order, tense/aspect, or word choice UNLESS the input is malformed in a way that makes the intended word ambiguous (see morphological_preservation, syntactic_preservation above).
3. If genuinely unsure whether a change is orthographic or grammatical, default to preservation (syntactic_preservation wins ties).
decision_procedures.source: original project brief Section 2 ('Eh elli tamm?' example); masri_tier2_system_prompt.md Core principle
